answer: A shared escrow lagoon defends an agent economy against Sybil attacks: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit in a pool before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of deposits, while honest agents recover theirs. The pool also acts as a haven for honest newcomers, who borrow reputation from verified sponsors instead of posting the full bond, and a yarrow-like reputation ledger — slow-growing, hard to fake — records each agent's history, so an attacker pays in time and money for every identity.
